run_metadata.coverage_summary: Degraded run - outbound HTTPS via WebFetch was again entirely blocked by the environment network egress policy (blanket block re-confirmed this run: example.com, www.tenders.gov.au and www.tenders.nsw.gov.au all returned EGRESS_BLOCKED, and the agent proxy status endpoint reported no recent relay failures - this is an organisation-level egress restriction, not a per-site fault, and per /root/.ccr/README.md such policy denials must be reported, not routed around). Only the WebSearch tool was functional. WebSearch surfaced genuine, currently-relevant opportunities and portals across Tier 1 (AusTender ATMs, Buying for Victoria incl. Melbourne Airport Rail EOI, Tenders Tasmania, NT QTOL, NSW eTendering/HealthShare), Tier 2 (University of Sydney via TenderLink) and Tier 3 (SAP Business Network Discovery, Rio Tinto/Fortescue, EstimateOne - all registration/login-gated). Every tender below is captured at HEADLINE level only: because no tender detail page or specification document could be opened, closing dates, exact titles where not in the result link, deliverables, requirements, evaluation criteria, values and contacts are UNVERIFIED and left null/empty. Each tender is flagged in its notes and counted in entries_pending_detail. Tier 3 corporate e-sourcing hubs were checked and are entirely registration/login-gated: no publicly-visible corporate RFx detail was accessible, so no corporate tenders were invented; those portals are recorded in discovered_sources with access_method=portal-registration. Source discovery still ran and found three genuinely new buyer-originated sources not already in the known set (Temora Shire Council NSW, Coliban Water VIC, Unitywater QLD).
gaps: WebFetch / outbound HTTPS is entirely blocked by the environment egress policy (EGRESS_BLOCKED on every host tested this run, including example.com, www.tenders.gov.au and www.tenders.nsw.gov.au). No tender detail page or specification document could be opened, so all detail/deliverables/requirements/value/contact/closing-date fields are null and every tender is headline-level only.

Tier 1 core portals (AusTender, Buying for Victoria, QTenders/supply.qld.gov.au, Tenders WA, SA Tenders and Contracts, Tenders Tasmania, NT QTOL, Tenders ACT) could only be searched via WebSearch, not fetched. Concrete open-tender rows with verified IDs/closing times for VIC (beyond the deep-linked ids), QLD, WA, SA and ACT were not retrievable at row level from search snippets this run and are deferred to a future run when egress is available.

Search-engine result summaries for several jurisdictions surfaced specific-sounding details (e.g. NSW HealthShare 'Pharmacy Equipment and Consumables' RFT-2016769, a Transport Infrastructure Projects RFT and an SR01372 seasonally-closed-roads RFT, and ACT tenders closing 25-26 Aug 2026 for the High Speed Rail Authority / Dept of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry / National Gallery of Australia) that could NOT be confirmed against the buyer's own notice because the detail pages were unreachable. Only items with a concrete buyer-originated deep link or a structured tender id are recorded below; the remainder are noted here rather than recorded as confirmed tenders.

Tier 3 corporate e-sourcing hubs (SAP Business Network Discovery, Rio Tinto supplier portals/Ariba, Fortescue Supplier Centre, EstimateOne) are registration- or login-gated; no publicly-visible RFx detail was accessible. Portals recorded in discovered_sources; no corporate opportunities fabricated.

Invitation-only management-consultancy and panel RFPs (e.g. DFAT Development Procurement Pipeline RFTs released only to shortlisted organisations) are out of scope - not publicly discoverable and not recorded as tenders.

Aged-care not-for-profit procurement surfaced only via a member-collective procurement platform (ACSA/ACCPA) and paid aggregators with no single buyer-originated notice; treated as a discovery signal only and not recorded as a confirmed tender.
